scope: One exposed historical tuning case; assessor-only addendum. Original submissions, scores, gates, cost estimates and denominators unchanged. No product change, paid calls or fresh confirmation.
finding: A bounded sign relation plus six fixed examples detects both authentic pre-fix hunks with fewer assertion lines. It does not establish exhaustive test equivalence, lower PR cost or a blind win.

source.merge_difference: Same sign changes; retains the old infinity comment.

property.domain: Positive magnitudes; numeric-first pairs of the listed specifiers; no leading literal, unit-only format or outer width/alignment. Ordinary specifier zero-padding is retained.
property.limits: Six independent expected examples anchor finite/infinite and integer behavior; they are not independent positive oracles for every matrix element. NaN, negative zero, extreme ranges and locale variants are outside this assay.

comparison.counting: Complete newly added TEST bodies; property includes its helper and six examples. Assertion lines include wrapped macro bodies. Stock already has a table-driven infinity test.
comparison.coverage_limit: Equal detection of two real regression classes only. Retaining separate boundary examples can erase the small whole-file line advantage over the merge.

outcomes.interpretation: Zero means every block in that group passed; positive counts are actual failed blocks. All initial processes exit1 because a separate invalid-x boundary expectation fails; a passing property group is not a whole-process pass.

negative_controls.rule: Apply one unique replacement at a time to a fresh merged copy; verify the restored lines against the base. These are the two original production hunks, not invented mutations.

initial_invalid_input.classification: Assay expectation error, not a valid sign counterexample. The initial failed boundary block and receipts are retained; corrected boundary checks also assert this exception.

runtime.mode: C++17, normal header-only fmt, freshly compiled original assertions, upstream GoogleTest entry

steps: Materialize literal base Git blobs from the pinned repository, including include/ and bundled test/gtest/. Verify all16 base headers against their blobs.

For each archived role select case_id=fmt and that role, verify UTF-8 patch bytes against source.patches, then apply from an independent Git root. Verify merged chrono.h against the pinned merged blob.

Extract only the two added TEST(chrono_test, name) blocks named in source.added_tests, preserving assertions. Rename suite chrono_test to archive_<role>. Combine all three suites with the property and a GoogleTest main.

Build each implementation from its own include/ directory. Link the prepared GoogleTest scaffolding; alternatively rebuild the bundled gmock-gtest-all.cc with the same pinned toolchain. Do not link a stale fmt binary.
Repeat with each authentic one-hunk reversion in a separate merged copy. Check group outcomes separately; the original mixed driver also included the documented invalid-x boundary expectation.
Independently check the corrected boundary cases and invalid-format exception on archived control headers. No outcome here replaces an original benchmark stage.
replay.receipt_hashes: Hashes identify retained original bytes; source/status replay is portable, while binary hashes or byte-identical logs across different build paths are not required.

limitations: Deterministic finite enumeration illustrates property testing; no JavaScript fast-check dependency, random generation or shrinking was used.
Full upstream chrono suite was not rebuilt or reexecuted.

An interrupted lease-wait controller later repeated base and overwrote the aggregate receipt. Outcomes were recovered from each retained XML/log; no complete allocation/timing ledger or time/cost saving is claimed.
Only disjoint existing CPU leases0-1/4-5 were used; CPUs6-7 were left to the ongoing workload. No product/proposal/score edits or paid calls.
